**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user is studying International Business.
- [FACT] The user has some experience in marketing and writing.
- [FACT] The user’s monthly income is around $2,500 AUD from a scholarship.
- [CHANGE] The user transferred all funds from their old bank account back home to a new Australian bank account on April 1st.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is concerned about overspending on food while getting used to prices in Melbourne.
- [EVENT] The user plans to start by updating their resume and LinkedIn profile.
- [EVENT] The user is considering getting a part-time job to supplement their scholarship.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant congratulated the user on taking the first step towards getting their finances in order and offered to help set up a budget for living expenses in Melbourne.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested categorizing expenses into Essential Expenses (Needs) and Non-Essential Expenses (Wants).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of Essential Expenses, including rent, utilities, food, transportation, insurance, minimum debt repayment, and phone/internet.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of Non-Essential Expenses, including entertainment, savings, personal care, gifts, and miscellaneous expenses.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended allocating 50-60% of income to Essential Expenses, 30-40% to Non-Essential Expenses, and 10-20% to Savings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested tracking expenses for a month using budgeting apps like Mint or You Need a Budget (YNAB).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for saving money on groceries, including meal planning, shopping at affordable supermarkets, buying in bulk, shopping at local markets, using cashback apps, and avoiding shopping when hungry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for saving money on dining out, including cooking at home, looking for deals, using food delivery apps wisely, eating at ethnic restaurants, and packing lunch.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested using the 50/30/20 rule for budgeting and setting a specific food budget.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant discussed the potential benefits of a part-time job, including increased income, gaining work experience, and improving time management.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised checking scholarship terms regarding part-time work and suggested a realistic work commitment of 10-15 hours per week.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant calculated potential additional income from a part-time job at $15-20 AUD per hour for 12 hours a week, totaling $720-960 AUD per month.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant
